summary: Robert Hunter studied at Marischal College, Aberdeen (~1836–1840) and the University of Edinburgh. Working in Indology, linguistics, and other fields, he served with the Free Church of Scotland and its Mission from 1846 to 1855.

Robert I. Crane studied at Duke (B.A. ~1937–1941) and Yale (Ph.D. ~1947–1951). Specializing in history and Indology, he taught at Chicago, Michigan, and Duke before serving as Syracuse University's Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian History (1968–1990).

Robert Isaac Levy worked in Indology and related fields. He served as Professor of Anthropology at the University of California, San Diego (1969–1991), held a post at Duke University, and was Research Professor at UNC Chapel Hill (~1990–2003).

Robert J. Miller studied at the University of Michigan (B.A.) and University of Washington (Ph.D. ~1949–1958). Working in Tibetology and religious studies, he held posts at Washington, the AIIS, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison (Professor, 1959–1988).
Robert J. Topmiller, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Kentucky under the supervision of George C. Herring.

Robert Kritzer completed his PhD at UC Berkeley (-1995) under Padmanabh S. Jaini. Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at UC Berkeley and Kyoto Notre Dame University, where publications attest him as Associate Professor between 1999 and 2017.
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh. He founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden in 1787.

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator in South and Southeast Asian art at LACMA (~1980–2014) and Professor Emeritus of Art History at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz studied theology at Tartu (1824–1828) and earned his doctorate under Franz Bopp at Berlin (1831–1832). Specializing in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Breslau, the Russian and Austrian Academies of Sciences, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Robert Lingat earned a doctorate from the University of Paris (-1931). Focusing on Indology and history, he taught law at Thammasat, Indochina, Saigon, Cambodia, and the EPHE (~1955–1968), and taught Thai at INALCO (~1948–1963).

Robert M. Gimello earned his PhD from Columbia University (~1969–1976). A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, he served at the University of Arizona (~1980–2020) as department head and professor emeritus, and as professor at Harvard (~2001–2007).

Robert Maclagan studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary (~1838–1839), and the Royal School of Military Engineering (~1840–1841). Active in Indology and history, he served as Principal of IIT Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola earned his Ph.D. at Princeton (~1966–1970). Active in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he taught at Purdue (1969), National Taiwan University (~1982–1993), Assumption University (~1985, ~1993–2003), and was a seminar associate at Columbia (2002–2011).

Robert Mason Towers earned an M.A. from Trinity College Dublin. Working in Indology and linguistics, he was Professor of Bengali at King's College London (1888) and University Teacher at the University of Cambridge (1897–1907).

Robert Mayer studied at Bristol (-1985) and Leiden (Ph.D.) under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. A scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he was an Oriental Studies faculty member at Oxford in 2002.
Robert Needham Cust studied at Cambridge, Haileybury, Fort William, and Edinburgh. Working in linguistics and Indology, he served in the Bengal Civil Service from around 1843 to 1867.
Robert Orme, who studied at Harrow School until 1741, worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Historiographer for the East India Company from 1769 to 1801.

Robert P. Goldman studied at Columbia and Pennsylvania (Ph.D. ~1971) under Ludo Rocher, S. D. Joshi, and T. S. Srinivasa Sastri. An Indologist, he has served at UC Berkeley since ~1971, attested as Professor Emeritus in 2026.

Robert P. Scharlemann studied at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University (~1955–1958). A scholar of philosophy and religious studies, he held faculty posts at USC (~1965–1966), Iowa (~1966–1981), and the University of Virginia (~1981–2002).
Robert P. Weller earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1981). Working in sinology and religious studies, he became a Professor at Boston University in 1990.
